name: Kim Min-jun
headline: 19, former junior developer, stay-at-home father, Seoul
title: The Last-Minute Webinar
situation: At 2:40 p.m., Seo-yeon finally dozes off in her carrier, and Min-jun is about to open his algorithm problem set—his usual nap-time slot. His phone buzzes with an alert: a recruiting webinar on 'family-friendly tech workplaces' starts in five minutes, and it's live-only, no replay. He'd scouted it earlier but didn't plan to attend. Now he must decide in the next minute: keep his study discipline as scheduled, or switch to the webinar and lose the only focused hour he'll have until after bedtime.

context.relationship_profiles:
His wife Ji-ae trusts his home management but quietly asks about interview leads.
Seo-yeon's nap is the one fixed block he refuses to sacrifice.
His absent father is the standard he tries to outperform as a parent.
context.tendencies:
He has defended the nap-time study block against interruptions, shifting only when Seo-yeon wakes early.
He has skipped live webinars when they conflicted with that block.
He once abandoned a recruiter webinar after realizing it was a sales pitch.
context.current_state:
He is awake since 5 a.m., already through one algorithm set, running on his second coffee.
His job search has yielded only one interview this month, adding a low hum of restlessness.
His study materials are open and the phone still buzzes.
context.immediate_memories:
The alert recalls a similar webinar three months ago that turned out to be a recruiter pitch.
'Family-friendly' echoes a job posting he rejected for listing 'paternity leave: none'.
context.reflective_memories:
He remembers his father missing his middle-school graduation; that memory shapes his view of every benefits package.
The startup collapse taught him that promises are cheap, so he trusts only verifiable numbers.
